name: Pembrolizumab (single agent)
cyclesNote: Continue until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or about 2 years (35 cycles at 200 mg every 3 weeks). A 400 mg every-6-weeks schedule is an accepted alternative.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Pembrolizumab is a PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor used in metastatic urothelial carcinoma after platinum-based chemotherapy in immunotherapy-naive patients. No companion biomarker is required in the post-platinum setting.

supportiveCare: Monitor for immune-related adverse events across organ systems (skin, colon, liver, endocrine glands, lungs, kidney); manage with holds and corticosteroids per severity.
Baseline and periodic thyroid, adrenal, and glucose assessment for endocrinopathies.
Educate the patient to report new diarrhea, dyspnea, jaundice, or rash promptly.
monitoring: thyroid function (TSH/free T4) at baseline and periodically
liver function before each cycle (immune hepatitis)
clinical assessment for colitis, pneumonitis, dermatitis, and endocrinopathy each visit

doseModificationRules.text: Hold pembrolizumab and start corticosteroids for grade 2-3 immune-related toxicity; resume after recovery to grade <= 1 and steroid taper. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 4 or recurrent grade 3 immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Permanently discontinue for grade 4 or recurrent severe immune-related toxicity per labeling; obtain specialty review.

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab
drugs.notes: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV flat dose on day 1 of a 21-day cycle. An alternative flat schedule gives 400 mg IV every 6 weeks. Standard checkpoint-inhibitor immune-related toxicity monitoring applies. Dose per standard urothelial practice (Standard Guidelines / DeVita / Harrison, general reference).

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, post-platinum immunotherapy
